episode_title: Pacific Lawn Sprinklers Franchise Radio Show Interview

real_qa.q: What is Pacific Lawn Sprinklers business model and how many franchisees does it currently operate?
real_qa.r: Pacific Lawn Sprinklers was founded 45 years ago by three brothers focused on the irrigation space. It began franchising in 2002 not primarily for national growth, but to incentivize employees to own their own territories. Currently, the company has 52 franchisees operating across 73 territories. The business model includes four revenue streams: irrigation installation, blowouts, breakage and maintenance, plus permanent lighting, holiday lighting, and drainage solutions—all demand-driven by franchisees who recognized cross-selling opportunities when already on customer properties.
real_qa.requete: Pacific Lawn Sprinklers franchisees territories revenue streams

real_qa.q: What is Pacific Lawn Sprinklers NPS score and how does it compare to other major brands?
real_qa.r: Pacific Lawn Sprinklers achieved an NPS score of 93%, which Riverside Group confirmed is the highest in their history across six different umbrella companies with almost 40 brands. For context, major companies like Apple score in the 80s, and other well-known brands typically score in the high 70s, making a 90s NPS score exceptionally rare and described as unicorn status.
real_qa.requete: Pacific Lawn Sprinklers NPS score 93 percent

real_qa.q: What are the ideal franchise candidate characteristics and investment range for Pacific Lawn Sprinklers?
real_qa.r: While historically owner-operators were ideal, Pacific Lawn Sprinklers now prioritizes sales and marketing professionals wanting to build an empire, plus HR-related individuals willing to engage in their community through B&I networking, local sponsorships, and customer-facing leadership. The franchisee hires irrigation technicians who only need to be handy, as the company trains them. Investment ranges from $100,000 to $150,000 with less than $100,000 going directly to the franchisor. The model is home-based requiring minimal employees—one person can generate significant revenue.
real_qa.requete: Pacific Lawn Sprinklers franchise investment cost ideal candidate

real_qa.q: What distinguishes Pacific Lawn Sprinklers from other irrigation franchises in the market?
real_qa.r: Pacific Lawn Sprinklers differentiates through a 55-person call center in New York that seamlessly manages franchisee schedules and customer appointments—unique in the franchising space. They offer optional bookkeeping services allowing franchisees to focus on sales, marketing, hiring, and staff retention. The four revenue streams reduce seasonality perception versus irrigation-only competitors. Additionally, every state is becoming stricter on water conservation, and Pacific Lawn emphasizes proper equipment and technology to manage this effectively, capabilities mom-and-pop operators typically lack.
real_qa.requete: Pacific Lawn Sprinklers call center competitive advantage differentiator

real_qa.q: How does Joel Lazarevitz structure the qualification and onboarding process for Pacific Lawn Sprinklers franchise candidates?
real_qa.r: The process begins with a personal call where Joel understands the candidate's motivation and expectations, confirming they can commit full-time. A second call covers a detailed webinar on the business model and nuts-and-bolts operations. Next, candidates receive the franchise disclosure document to review. If still interested, they're introduced to existing franchisees and the brand leader Mary Mahoney (30 years with the company), then ideally travel to New York for a full day meeting. Training itself includes virtual onboarding, four to five days at the Long Island training facility, and post-training ride-alongs with a dedicated franchise business coach in the candidate's community.
real_qa.requete: Pacific Lawn Sprinklers franchise qualification process training onboarding

guest.bio_context: Joel has been in franchising since 1997, accumulating 27 years of experience. He started in children's enrichment education, growing a company from Montreal to 225 franchises across 25 countries, then launched his own fractional development consulting firm. Over his career, he has introduced brands to over 65 countries and 150+ US cities, focusing exclusively on service-based businesses. Most recently, Maid Brigade was acquired by Riverside Group 14 months ago, and he was subsequently offered the role managing Pacific Lawn Sprinklers, a 45-year-old irrigation franchise.
